title: Resynchronize private cluster SSO session assertions with KMS rotation to restore RBAC and audit continuity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers using Private deployments reported RBAC failures and missing audit events coincident with KMS envelope rotations. Investigation shows long-lived SSO session assertions (NameID + groups) were not being revalidated against new key envelopes, and the KMS rotation path suppressed audit emission for transient internal tokens. Result: role bindings drifted and audit trails omitted several service-access events during rotation windows.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy private cluster with external IdP (SAML) and long-lived session proxy enabled.
2) Establish long-running requests that reuse session assertions via the session cache/prefix.
3) Trigger KMS envelope rotation (rotate-envelopes API or simulate key rollover from control plane).
4) Observe: API calls using cached assertions succeed but now map to stale role claims; audit log entries for KMS envelope unwrap and assertion rekey are missing in control-plane audit stream.
5) Confirm with customer logs: missing audit events within rotation time window and RBAC policy engine returning fallback roles for affected sessions.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - Pager: multiple private customers opened escalations referencing missing 'kms.unwrap' audit events.
2026-03-10 11:04 UTC - Initial debug: reproduced in staging by forcing envelope rotation; root reproduction matched customer reports.
2026-03-10 16:30 UTC - Found code path: session validation middleware skips revalidation when session token signature verifies against old envelope if stable KV cache present.

2026-03-11 08:20 UTC - KMS team: documented that envelope rotation path marks tokens as 'transient' and previously skipped emitting audit events for internal unwraps to avoid noise. This suppression caused missing control-plane audit records.
2026-03-11 13:45 UTC - Security review: risk assessment indicates potential compliance violation for customers with strict audit retention/SOC2 requirements. Escalated to Product and Legal.

2026-03-12 03:10 UTC - Decided to prepare a minimal hotpatch that: forces assertion revalidation on envelope rotation boundaries, re-enables audit emission for unwrap events that affect session-to-role mapping, and schedules a background backfill of missed audit entries.

2026-03-12 09:55 UTC - Trade-offs discussed: emitting all internal unwraps increases control-plane audit noise and cost; scoped solution emits unwrap events only when session/token mapping or role claims are impacted. Agreed by Security and Observability.
2026-03-12 15:40 UTC - QA repro: added an automated scenario in CI that simulates rotation and asserts audit event presence and RBAC consistency.
patch_summary: patch: controlplane/session_validate: on detection of recent KMS envelope rotation for a tenant, invalidate cached assertion->role mapping and re-run SAML attribute mapping path.
patch: kms/unwrap: restore conditional audit emission for unwrap events when unwrap is used to validate session assertions or when unwrap changes key fingerprint used for signing assertions.
patch: session-proxy/cache: add TTL bump and rotation-bound marker to avoid silent continuity across rotations.
tests: add integration test 'rotation-rbac-continuity' and unit tests for unwrap audit conditionalization.
docs: update private-deploy/runbooks with rotation checklist and how to run the audit backfill tool.
rollout_plan: 1) Build runtime-1.21-hotfix branch and create CI artifact.
2) Canary deploy to dedicated internal staging-private cluster with two tenant customers emulated (03:00 UTC window). Monitor RBAC correctness and audit event rate.
3) After 60 minutes of stability and verification of backfill job run, escalate canary to 10% of affected private clusters (non-prod customers) for 2 hours.
4) If no regressions, schedule customer-facing private clusters update in waves: small (<10 tenants), medium (10-100), large (>100) with 30m observation windows.
5) Rollback plan: revert to prior runtime artifact and trigger emergency backfill to mark affected sessions as invalid and force re-authentication if RBAC anomalies persist.
6) Communicate planned windows to customers and provide an opt-out for immediate reauth enforcement.
qa_checks: - Integration test passes: rotation-rbac-continuity in CI.
- Canary cluster: no more than 2% increase in audit ingestion rate after conditionalization (expected), RBAC mapping mismatch counters drop to 0 for reproduced case.
- Security sign-off: security-team@redwood.ai approves patch on 2026-03-12.
- Conformance test: SAML NameID normalization tests pass for multiple IdP name formats.
postmortem_actions: - Implement telemetry to detect rotation-bound session reuse and trigger proactive reauth guidance to customers.
- Add an automated backfill job to reconstruct missing audit records within 72 hours of rotation if suppression occurred.
- Update runbooks: clearly list steps to verify audit continuity after KMS rotation and to safely run customer-facing backfills.
- Plan: longer-term redesign to record minimal unwrap metadata for every rotation to avoid conditional logic that can produce gaps.
